title: Grouping and layout
description: Four ways of deciding what a group is, against a hand-written CSV (top row), plus the three routes to a real topology proven against the live dev cluster (label, join, ranges), and a panel that is deliberately incomplete to exercise the coverage warning.

panels.title: By a label, in rack layout
panels.description: The best case: the exporter already publishes the structure. Rack layout stacks each group as a chassis instead of wrapping it. The rack column in this CSV is hand-written: slurm_exporter publishes no such label, and there is nowhere for one to come from because it reads sinfo. Grouping by a label is only available if you add the label yourself, through Prometheus relabelling or a join against an inventory.

panels.title: By a capture, splitting compute from GPU
panels.description: Not a location grouping, and it no longer pretends to be one: the dev cluster's node names are flat (c1..c160, g1..g80) with nothing encoding a rack, so '^([a-z]+)' recovers only the node's class - compute or GPU - not its position on the floor. That is genuinely useful on its own, which is why the panel stays, but do not read it as the realistic answer for topology; the live-Prometheus panels below (label, join, ranges) are that answer, because they read from something outside the node name.

panels.title: Rung 1 -- label, against live Prometheus
panels.description: Rung 1 of three routes to the same topology: slurm_node_status carries a real rack label because dev/relabel/racks.txt was turned into Prometheus relabelling by make scrape. Grouping > Group by > Label needs nothing else. Same 15-node slice as the join and ranges panels beside it, so all three can be compared directly.

panels.title: Rung 2 -- join, against an inventory the metrics do not carry
panels.description: Rung 2 of three routes to a topology, and the one available to anyone whose Prometheus carries no location dimension at all: query A reads slurm_node_status live with Format set to Table, so Prometheus hands back one row per node instead of one frame per series; query B is a hand-maintained CSV inventory (node,zone) against the TestData source, naming a zone that exists nowhere in the scraped metrics. The panel's own datasource is set to -- Mixed --, which is what makes Grafana actually run a query-B target when the panel datasource is Prometheus. Join by field (byField node, mode outer) merges the two into one frame, whose refId becomes "joinByField-A-B" rather than "A", which is why Data > State query points at that name rather than the query's own refId. Grouping by "zone" rather than "rack" is deliberate: a value that only the join could have supplied is proof the join ran, not an assertion resting on which of two agreeing columns Grafana happened to keep.

panels.title: Rung 3 -- ranges, against live Prometheus
panels.description: Rung 3 of three routes to the same topology: no rack label and no join, just a range table typed into the panel and held in the $racks dashboard variable. Same 15-node slice as the label and join panels beside it.

panels.title: Deliberately incomplete -- a range table covering one rack of six
panels.description: Not a bug: this panel's range table names only rack1: c[1-40], against the full 240-node cluster. 200 nodes match no range and are drawn under "ungrouped", dashed and marked unplaced, and the warnings strip both names them and reports that the rack label would cover all 240, the coverage signal the other panels never trigger, because every source they use already covers every node. Its warnings strip is deliberate too, not a defect: a reader could otherwise mistake the coverage line for something broken, which is why the title already says "Deliberately incomplete".

panels.title: Blades -- a mixed floor, against live Prometheus
panels.description: Blade density, against live Prometheus. Nodes per blade, by group puts four densities on one floor: the four compute racks take quad blades, rack5 and rack6 triples, rack7 single-node servers, and the two gpu racks duos - so a cabinet is drawn four, three, one or two sleds wide. rack7's line restates the default of 1 on purpose: a floor plan that names every cabinet reads better than one where the quiet ones are inferred. Every cabinet is twenty slots and every one is full, because the fixture sizes a rack at twenty times its density rather than giving them all the same node count. Declared heights that differ are panel 10's job.

panels.title: A declaration too small for what arrived
panels.description: rack1 is declared at four slots and the query returns forty nodes. The panel draws all forty: the thirty-six that do not fit spill above the frame's top edge rather than being truncated, because a node that exists and is not drawn is a node nobody is watching. The warnings strip says so. This panel exists to pin the direction of that spill and the clearance above it, which jsdom cannot see.

panels.title: Two declared heights, one floor
panels.description: Slots per rack, by group, against live Prometheus. Both cabinet kinds draw twenty rows here - eighty compute nodes at four per blade, forty gpu nodes at two - so the only thing separating their heights is the declaration: twenty slots against twenty-six. A cabinet's height is a property of the hardware, not of what is currently plugged into it, and the gpu cabinets are drawn with six empty slots above their last row rather than shrunk to fit. Both kinds still stand on the same floor: a short cabinet sits on it, it does not hang from the ceiling. That is the defect this option exists to fix, and the e2e suite measures it on this panel.
